output.reason: Sudden, painless, persistent monocular vision loss two hours ago in a 55-year-old is a possible central retinal artery occlusion or retinal detachment, both requiring immediate emergency assessment.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Sudden painless loss of vision in one eye that hasn't returned can be a blocked retinal artery — treated as a stroke of the eye — or a retinal detachment, and both need urgent eye and stroke assessment today. Have someone drive you rather than driving yourself. If you develop face droop, weakness, numbness or trouble speaking, call 911 immediately.
differential: Central retinal artery occlusion (retinal stroke equivalent)
Retinal detachment or other acute retinal vascular event
